reading.body:
Microsoft operates a data center campus in Warren County that spans three counties in central Iowa. The company does not publish megawatt capacity, square footage, or building count for individual campuses, disclosing only aggregate global statistics. The Warren County facility is one component of the West Des Moines campus, which Microsoft has reported investing $1.5 to $2 billion to build, with a sixth data center reported as planned.

Among Iowa's 52 mapped data center facilities, only two operators publish individual campus capacity figures. This campus ranks third by published megawatt capacity in the state, though its own capacity remains undisclosed. The state total for published capacity is 18 megawatts across all facilities.

The absence of published specifications makes it impossible to assess what this campus means for AI scaling without additional reporting. The investment scale and multi-county footprint suggest material infrastructure, but translation into racks, accelerators, or grid load requires assumptions Microsoft has chosen not to provide. The planned sixth building indicates continued expansion, but the company's disclosure policy leaves the campus's role in AI compute capacity opaque.
